name: Remote-managed home cleaning business
one_liner: Run a residential cleaning company from home: you handle marketing, booking and quality control, and subcontracted cleaners do the work, even in a city where you don't live.
customer: Homeowners and busy households who want recurring or one-off home cleaning
offer: Recurring and one-off residential cleaning, with window cleaning as an add-on or entry offer
how_it_makes_money: Per-clean or recurring service fees. The operator keeps the margin between the price charged and what the subcontracted cleaners are paid. Video 8XSaVl6QnVA claims about $373/day; Allan's business is described as $29K/month.
startup_cost: low (no amount stated; the model needs no equipment and no employees, and Allan started window cleaning with a water-fed pole)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown (Allan got early jobs by knocking on doors; probably weeks)
evidence: Allan 'runs a company, a remote cleaning business, actually not in the state' (he lives in Vegas) - Nc-1LMAwYYo

risks: Inconsistent cleaner quality and high churn
Customer complaints still need handling, often by phone
Local competition and the cost of getting customers

how_it_makes_money: Monthly retainers per client. The agency is described as making $3M/year after about 7 years.
startup_cost: low (no amount stated; it started from the founder's own LinkedIn presence)
time_to_first_revenue: unknown (the founder built his own LinkedIn brand first, then took clients)
